hidden_run_story_state.taboo: do not ring a bridge bell without witness

recurring_motifs: white plaster handprints used as witness counts
bell tongues wrapped in linen and stored like relics
double seals showing civic law beside devotional correction
upturned bowls marking unblessed or tainted water
vine-cut slit arrows pointing toward the sealed cistern stair

nook_packets.survival_use: reliquary shelf for wrapped bell tongues and witness petitions
nook_packets.material_context: plaster niche, soot rim, wrapped bronze tongues, ash wax, white handprint counts
nook_packets.survival_pressure: the old call-to-order is gone, so authority must be reassembled through substitute rites
nook_packets.taboo_or_rule: no tongue is struck without three witnessed hands
text_fragments: Tongue of the third bell. Wrapped in salt cloth. Do not unwrap without two witnesses.
If the wrapping is dry, record it. If wet, report to the quartermaster before touching.
Seven tongues stored. Three unaccounted. Tally stands until route opens.
symbol_fragments: three white palm marks beside the same wrapped tongue
crossed-out ring marks under newer witness dots
nook_packets.absence_or_interruption: the largest bell tongue is wrapped twice, as if too dangerous or too sacred to expose.
nook_packets.location_hint: high on the shrine rim wall beside a dead bell line
nook_packets.voice_note: A caretaker's inventory note under pressure of dwindling accountability, where the act of wrapping substitutes for the act of ringing.

nook_packets.survival_use: teaching step where children learn witness law before bell routes
nook_packets.material_context: chalk panel, child-height step marks, folded wraps, cracked prayer stool
nook_packets.survival_pressure: children must know how to move through sacred infrastructure without triggering old dangers
nook_packets.taboo_or_rule: you may draw the witness mark before you may touch the bell rope
evidence_objects: stool worn smooth on one side
text_fragments: Stand on the marked step. Say your name aloud. Wait for the echo. That is witness enough.
Children: do not skip the step. The step is the rule now.
No echo means the passage is blocked again. Mark the date on the post.
symbol_fragments: child-drawn circles around handprints
lesson arrows cut short at the sealed stair
nook_packets.absence_or_interruption: the last lesson line ends before the word 'ring'.
nook_packets.location_hint: on the inner stair before the upper lantern court
nook_packets.voice_note: A work captain's instruction simplified for novices and children after formal witness rites could no longer be staffed.

nook_packets.survival_use: bench for forging exemptions, devotional countersigns, and witness-valid route papers
nook_packets.material_context: stamp tray, wax knives, chalk corrections, lead seal scraps, white plaster dust
nook_packets.survival_pressure: old civic authority still blocks movement, so sanctuary requires document and ritual both
nook_packets.taboo_or_rule: every civic seal must be answered by a witnessed mercy mark
evidence_objects: wax blade used for both law and devotion
text_fragments: Both seals must press wet. One seal alone is a draft, not a record.
Civic seal left. Devotional seal right. Order is not optional.
If the devotional stamp is cracked, use the copy stamp. Note the substitution in the margin.
symbol_fragments: square customs stamp beside round handprint mark
same docket amended in two inks
nook_packets.absence_or_interruption: the official bronze stamp is missing, but its dust square remains exact.
nook_packets.location_hint: at the old toll bench beneath the shrine ledger shelf
nook_packets.voice_note: A refugee clerk's procedural reminder, insisting on legitimacy through form when institutional authority has already fractured.

nook_packets.survival_use: triage point for water judged safe, tainted, or unblessed
nook_packets.material_context: ceramic bowls, water drip marks, bowl lids turned upside down, measure lines on plaster
nook_packets.survival_pressure: ritual purity and bodily safety have diverged since the cistern routes failed
nook_packets.taboo_or_rule: an upturned bowl is touched only by those already marked for bitter water
evidence_objects: upright and inverted bowls in strict rows
chalk taste marks on the wall
text_fragments: Bowls upturned: water inside is not cleared. Do not drink. Do not pour on offerings.
Three bowls waiting since the collapse. No one with standing to bless them has come.
Leave them upturned. Touching them counts as a claim. You do not want the claim.
symbol_fragments: triangle taste marks beside inverted bowls
measure lines cut deeper at the lower shelf
nook_packets.absence_or_interruption: one bowl row is empty except for a wet ring and a witness handprint.
nook_packets.location_hint: near the former washing arcade under the shrine rim
nook_packets.voice_note: A caretaker's warning to scavengers, where the upturned bowl has become a legal and ritual boundary marker simultaneously.

nook_packets.survival_use: silent memorial stop for those lost when routes failed and bells never sounded
nook_packets.material_context: arch shadow, witness handprints, ash line, token stones, cracked bell bracket
nook_packets.survival_pressure: the dead must be counted without invoking the bell that failed them
nook_packets.taboo_or_rule: touch the bracket, do not strike it
evidence_objects: ash rubbed into the old strike point
text_fragments: These names were never rung out. The bell fell before the list was read.
Do not ring a substitute here without a witness standing at the arc. That is the rule.
If you knew one of these names, press your hand to the plaster. That is permitted.
symbol_fragments: rows of handprints grouped by household
old ring circles darkened over with ash
nook_packets.absence_or_interruption: the strike hammer is gone, but the reach marks are fresh.
nook_packets.location_hint: in the shadow of the collapsed bell arch above the rim walkway
nook_packets.voice_note: A mourner's posted instruction, holding the memorial open through substitution while acknowledging the original rite was never completed.

nook_packets.survival_use: curtained sleep cell for those tending the upper rites and watching the sealed stair
nook_packets.material_context: curtain strips, low pallet, oil flask, bowl pair, folded witness cloth
nook_packets.survival_pressure: someone must keep continuous watch over the sealed cistern route while maintaining upper refuge quiet
nook_packets.taboo_or_rule: the watcher sleeps closest to the cloth, never to the bell line
text_fragments: Curtain closed means the cell is in use for substitute rite. Do not open it.
Curtain folded back and pinned: cell is empty and cleared. You may shelter here.
If the curtain is torn, the last occupant left in haste. Check the floor for dropped papers.
symbol_fragments: one upright bowl, one downturned bowl
curtain knot tied in witness-count pattern
nook_packets.absence_or_interruption: the oil flask is warm-stained, but the pallet has not been smoothed since the last watch.
nook_packets.location_hint: on the roof lane behind torn curtain cloth and a broken lantern rail
nook_packets.voice_note: A work captain's shorthand system for managing shared sanctuary space after formal room assignment collapsed.

nook_packets.survival_use: substitution wall where impossible rites are answered with household objects and written exceptions
nook_packets.material_context: plaster pockets, child shoes, ration tokens, clipped vine, old saint niches with new chalk notes
nook_packets.survival_pressure: the proper offerings no longer exist, but the need to answer grief and petition remains
nook_packets.taboo_or_rule: if the proper thing is gone, offer the thing that cost you sleep
evidence_objects: ration tokens tucked into saint niches
text_fragments: If you have no proper offering, fold your name and press it flat against the lower course.
Folded names are not lesser. They are the record now. Do not remove another's fold.
Wall is full at the third course. Begin the fourth course left to right, no gaps.
symbol_fragments: crossed saint halos with household marks beneath
same chalk line repeated under three empty niches
nook_packets.absence_or_interruption: one niche is polished bare, suggesting an object was taken back in desperation.
nook_packets.location_hint: along the inner shrine wall where votive shelves step upward
nook_packets.voice_note: A penitent's instruction that has quietly become administrative policy, spoken in the voice of someone who had to make the rule themselves.

nook_packets.survival_use: tool table for preparing a reopening attempt on the sealed water route
nook_packets.material_context: cap bolts, old wrench, chalk fit marks, vine-cut arrow tags, wrapped replacement washers
nook_packets.survival_pressure: if the cistern route can be reopened, the district may escape both thirst and bell-law dependence
nook_packets.taboo_or_rule: nothing is turned until the witness count matches the bolt count
evidence_objects: wrapped tool roll for a route not yet opened
text_fragments: Route papers for the cistern stair are held here. Do not take a paper without signing the ledger.
Cap is sealed. Papers are preparation only. Taking one is not permission to descend.
When the cap opens, the first ten names in the ledger go first. Add your name now.
symbol_fragments: bolt numbers beside handprint circles
arrow slits cut toward the sealed stair
nook_packets.absence_or_interruption: the final washer is missing, but its cloth wrap is already laid open on the table.
nook_packets.location_hint: beside the capped cistern stair above the old wash channel
nook_packets.voice_note: A refugee clerk managing hope as a queue, keeping the sealed route alive through bureaucratic anticipation rather than mystical promise.

nook_packets.survival_use: witness-count panel that doubles as ration and water priority order
nook_packets.material_context: plaster panel, charcoal columns, handprints, bowl-hook pegs, wiped-off names
nook_packets.survival_pressure: the district now allocates water and rite access by who can witness, carry, and survive the climb
nook_packets.taboo_or_rule: a handprint can stand where a name cannot
evidence_objects: empty pegs where bowl tags once hung
text_fragments: Each white print is one witness present at a rite since the collapse. Count them yourself.
If your hand is smaller than the prints, press anyway. Size is not the measure.
Panel is full when prints overlap three deep. Start the second panel on the east wall.
symbol_fragments: smallest handprints grouped beside lower water measures
one whole column scraped clean and re-counted
nook_packets.absence_or_interruption: an entire row is wiped away except for one thumb mark.
nook_packets.location_hint: on the panel wall before the upper cistern queue once formed
nook_packets.voice_note: A novice's copied instruction, preserving the witness-count system in the plainest possible terms after the original custodians were lost.

nook_packets.survival_use: whisper-rite nook where children learn the rhythm of a bell they may not ring
nook_packets.material_context: bench groove, chalk pulse marks, folded witness cloth strips, chipped pitch bowl
nook_packets.survival_pressure: rite memory must survive after the instrument and permission are both gone
nook_packets.taboo_or_rule: keep the rhythm in the hand, not the iron
evidence_objects: pitch bowl used as silent tempo marker
text_fragments: Sing facing the wall. The corner carries the sound. That is why this spot was chosen.
No bell, no lead voice. Begin on the third breath. Stop when the echo stops.
This is not performance. Do not watch the one singing. Turn away or leave.
symbol_fragments: even tap marks cut by small hands
tiny witness circles around a silent bowl
nook_packets.absence_or_interruption: the bowl lip is chipped where a clapper should have struck, but never did.
nook_packets.location_hint: in the blind choir corner behind the upper plaster screen
nook_packets.voice_note: A penitent's rule for a substitute choir rite, insisting on the correct posture of witness even when the original choir structure is gone.

nook_packets.survival_use: name concealment drawer where the dead are paired with witness cloth and age tags
nook_packets.material_context: linen bundles, age tags, ash dust, sealed slips, witness cloth tied in threes
nook_packets.survival_pressure: names are preserved physically even when they cannot be spoken or displayed openly
nook_packets.taboo_or_rule: the slip may be folded, never discarded
text_fragments: Names written on linen strips. One strip per person unaccounted since the collapse.
Do not add a name until three days have passed without word. That is the waiting rule.
Strips with a knot at the end: confirmed gone. Strips unknotted: still waiting.
symbol_fragments: three-knot witness ties
age tags arranged by climb order instead of kin
nook_packets.absence_or_interruption: one drawer is open and empty except for ash where a folded slip should be.
nook_packets.location_hint: under the sanctuary shelf where linen once waited for feast days
nook_packets.voice_note: A mourner's filing system that refuses to close grief prematurely, using the knot as the only honest marker of certainty.

nook_packets.survival_use: reserve shelf for oil, dry cloth, and bitter-water bowls kept for the sealed cistern attempt
nook_packets.material_context: lamp recess, oil flask, wrapped bowl stack, hidden shelf behind broken plaster, vine-slit arrow
nook_packets.survival_pressure: reopening the cistern route requires a staged cache and assumes some who start the climb will not finish it
nook_packets.taboo_or_rule: reserve stock is counted by returns, not departures
text_fragments: Vine cut points down and left. That is the stair direction. Mark it on your route paper.
Cache holds: two coils of rope, one lamp, four days of dry ration. Counted last at mid-season.
Do not open the cache for practice. It opens when the cap opens. Not before.
symbol_fragments: vine-cut arrow toward hidden shelf
return-count notches deeper than departure marks
nook_packets.absence_or_interruption: the brightest flask is missing, but the return notch for it was never cut.
nook_packets.location_hint: behind broken plaster beside the sealed cistern stair
nook_packets.voice_note: A quartermaster's terse field note, treating the sealed route as a logistical certainty rather than a hope, because someone has to believe it will open.
